newsitem.title: DENMARK: FORECAST - Denmark sees lower German bond yield gap.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Denmark sees lower German bond yield gap.

text.p: Denmark's Economy Ministry said in its economic survey issued on Tuesday that it expected the 10-year bond yield gap between Denmark and Germany to fall close to 50 basis points (bps) by end-1997.
It said it expected the gap to narrow to less than 50 bps on average in 1998 but gave no precise figure. On Tuesday, the differential was 89 basis points.
The government survey also forecast that the 10-year Danish benchmark bond will yield on average 7.2 percent at end-1996, fall to 6.7 percent next year and 6.6 percent in 1998.
Tuesday's yield on the benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was around 6.65 percent.
